gold.question: Regarding FV-107-3 on the P&ID: What's the Cv at full open for a 2 inch valve?

candidate: The datasheet for FV-107-3 (Fisher ET/D100022x012) does not give a single Cv labelled "at full open" for a 2 inch valve, but Table 17 (p. 23) lists maximum flow coefficients (Cv) at maximum valve plug travel (i.e., fully open, full-sized trim, equal percentage cage, normal flow direction) for a 2 inch valve depending on type/trim: EAT with liner 48.1, EAT without liner 47.2, ED 59.7, ETR 59.7. The standard ET variant is not listed for 2 inch in these facts.

gold.answer: HART 4-20 mA: if self-diagnostics detect a sensor or microprocessor failure, the output is driven high or low; the direction is user-selectable with a jumper/switch on the transmitter. Factory default is High alarm unless specified (CT = Rosemount standard low alarm, CN = NAMUR low, C4 = NAMUR high). Levels: default high >= 21.75 mA (>= 22.5 mA with M6, DA1, T9, RK), low <= 3.75 mA; NAMUR >= 22.5 / <= 3.6 mA; custom 20.2-23.0 / 3.6-3.8 mA. Output M: below 0.94 V or above 5.4 V, selectable by internal jumper. F, W, X: failure passed as alert and status.
must: high or low, user-selectable by jumper/switch
gold.question: Consider the transmitter that feeds controller FIC-10-2. When the transmitter fails, does the output go high or low, and how do I change that alarm direction?

candidate: The transmitter FT-10-2 that feeds FIC-10-2 is a Rosemount 3051-series transmitter. On a detected sensor or microprocessor failure, its analog output is driven either high or low to alert the user; which direction applies is user-selectable with a jumper/switch on the transmitter, and the actual alarm current levels depend on whether the unit is configured for standard (default), NAMUR-compliant, or custom alarm levels (for 4-20 mA HART output, e.g. default high alarm >= 21.75 mA and low alarm <= 3.75 mA). So the failure direction is not fixed: set it via the internal jumper/switch on the transmitter.

gold.answer: Suction 4" (102 mm), discharge 2 1/2" (64 mm), raised face flanges; so yes, 2 1/2" is the discharge. Suction flange 8 holes 0.75" on 7.50" bolt circle, discharge 4 holes 0.75" on 5.50" bolt circle; optional NPT companion flanges.
gold.question: Regarding P-1-3 on the P&ID: What size are the suction and discharge connections? Is the '2 1/2' the port size?

candidate: P-1-3 (Model VGH2 1/2C31-B, Gorman-Rupp datasheet gorman-rupp-0700286) has a pump size of 4" x 2 1/2" (102 x 64 mm). The 4-inch side is the suction port (optional 4.00-8 NPT companion flange listed under SUCTION, with an 8-hole raised-face flange, 7.50 in bolt circle), and the 2 1/2-inch side is the discharge port (optional 2.50-8 NPT companion flange listed under DISCHARGE, with a 4-hole flange, 5.50 in bolt circle). So yes, the 2 1/2 is a port size — but it is the discharge port size, not the suction. The P&ID itself does not note connection sizes for P-1-3.
